Monetary transmission mechanism or monetary transmission is the term used to describe the process by which decisions about monetary policy affect the economy as a whole and the dynamics of inflation in particular. It explains how the signal from the central bank about maintaining or changing interest rates and their future trajectory is gradually transmitted from individual segments of the financial market to the real sector of the economy and ultimately to inflation.
